function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a complete, ready‑to‑commit set of files that will give you a Docker image, a Kubernetes deployment/service, and a GitHub Actions workflow that builds the image whenever you push to `main`.  
Feel free to copy the snippets into the appropriate files in your repository.

---

## 1️⃣ Dockerfile (Node.js)

Create a file named `Dockerfile` at the root of the repo:

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Base image – Alpine is small and fast
FROM node:18-alpine

# Working directory inside the container
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies only
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port your app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Default command
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why this Dockerfile?**  
> * `node:18-alpine` is lightweight and contains everything you need to run a Node.js app.  
> * `npm ci` guarantees a clean install of the exact versions in `package-lock.json`.  
> * The container listens on port **3000** – adjust if your app uses a different port.

---

## 2️⃣ Kubernetes YAML

Create a file named `k8s.yaml` (or split into `deployment.yaml` & `service.yaml`) at the root of the repo:

```yaml
# k8s.yaml
# ------------------------------------
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- change if you use another registry
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - port: 80          # Service port exposed inside the cluster
    targetPort: 3000  # Container port
```

> **What this does**  
> * Deploys two replicas of your app.  
> * Exposes the app via a `ClusterIP` service on port 80 (you can change to `NodePort` or `LoadBalancer` if you need external access).

---

## 3️⃣ GitHub Actions Workflow

Create a file at `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
# ------------------------------------
name: CI/CD

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # 1️⃣ Checkout the repo
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      # 2️⃣ Set up Docker Buildx (multi‑platform support)
      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v2

      # 3️⃣ Log in to GitHub Container Registry (ghcr.io)
      - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@v2
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # 4️⃣ Build and push the Docker image
      - name: Build and push Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest
```

> **How it works**  
> * On every push to `main`, the workflow checks out the repo, builds the Docker image, and pushes it to **GitHub Container Registry** under the same name as the repo (`ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome`).  
> * No extra secrets are required because the workflow uses the built‑in `GITHUB_TOKEN`.

---

## 4️⃣ Add, Commit & Push

Open a terminal in the repo root and run:

```bash
# Stage the new/updated files
git add Dockerfile k8s.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml

# Commit with a descriptive message
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"

# Push to the remote repository
git push origin main
```

> **Tip** – If you already had a `Dockerfile` or `k8s.yaml`, make sure to review the changes before committing.  
> If you prefer separate YAML files, you can split `k8s.yaml` into `deployment.yaml` and `service.yaml` and adjust the `git add` command accordingly.

---

### 🎉 Done!

After pushing, you should see the new workflow run automatically in the **Actions** tab of your GitHub repo. The Docker image will be available at `ghcr.io/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest`, and you can deploy the Kubernetes manifests to any cluster that has access to that registry.
